title: Arrays, hashing and prefix sums
conceptCue: track frequencies or previously seen information; contiguous sums with signed values often need prefix sums.
pitfalls: confusing longest with count, overwriting earliest indexes, omitting prefix sum zero, assuming positive values.
cost: these standard approaches are O(n) expected time with hash tables; Kadane uses O(1) extra space, prefix maps up to O(n).
say: “The stored information represents all earlier prefixes; I query before inserting the current prefix.”
review: contrast a running optimum, set membership and prefix counting.

title: Sorting, two pointers and matrix indexing
conceptCue: order enables elimination or merging; a matrix transformation is an index mapping.
pitfalls: duplicate triplets, pointer progress, sorting mutation, square-matrix assumptions and merge counting boundaries.
cost: merge sort O(n log n) time/O(n) auxiliary space; standard quicksort average O(n log n), worst O(n²); sorted 3 Sum O(n²); square rotation O(n²) time/O(1) extra space in place.
say: “Once sorted, this comparison lets me discard this side.”
review: re-derive the pointer move or coordinate transform.

title: Binary search over indexes
conceptCue: a sorted interval or structured partition permits half the candidates to be removed.
pitfalls: mixing closed and half-open intervals, no progress at two elements, duplicates, assuming all matrix variants share ordering.
cost: bounds O(log n)/O(1); globally ordered flattened matrix O(log(rc))/O(1); duplicate-heavy rotated variants may degrade to O(n).
say: “My answer remains inside this interval after every update.”
review: trace empty, absent, first, last and duplicate cases permitted by the statement.

title: Binary search on an answer
conceptCue: a proposed capacity, rate or distance has a monotone feasibility test.
pitfalls: reversed monotonicity, invalid bounds, integer ceiling and impossible cases.
cost: commonly O(n log R) time for answer-range size R and O(1) working space; sorting may add O(n log n), such as cows.
say: “If this value is feasible, every larger/smaller value is also feasible because…”
review: prove the predicate before writing the search.

title: Recursion and backtracking
conceptCue: enumerate choices while carrying state and undoing changes.
pitfalls: missing base cases, sharing a mutable result, duplicate choices, reusing an index incorrectly, invalid positive-only pruning.
cost: subset enumeration has 2^n leaves and O(n·2^n) output size; other bounds depend on candidates and target. Avoid calling all recursion O(2^n).
say: “At this depth the choice means…, and the recursive call owns…”
review: draw three levels and state what is restored.

title: Linked lists
conceptCue: pointer changes, middle finding and cycles require explicit reference invariants.
pitfalls: losing the remainder, dereferencing null, changing a list unexpectedly, confusing node identity with equal values.
cost: the standard approaches are O(n+m) or O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space, assuming the applicable cycle/acyclic conditions.
say: “These pointers refer to the processed prefix, current node and untouched suffix.”
review: draw before/after arrows for lengths 1, 2 and 3; explain restoration for palindrome if required.

title: Bits and elementary number theory
conceptCue: bit counts/parity, XOR cancellation or factor/divisibility structure.
pitfalls: signed shifts, overflow, fixed-width assumptions, XOR not preserving order.
cost: fixed-width bit scans O(n·b), XOR range O(1), classic sieve O(N log log N) time/O(N) space, trial factorisation O(√N) worst-case time.
say: “This operation preserves exactly this frequency information.”
review: use tiny binary examples. B/C until array and control-flow basics are stable.

title: Greedy intervals and local choices
conceptCue: a choice can be proven safe by exchanging it with part of an optimal solution.
pitfalls: intuition without proof, touching endpoints, mixing minimum resources with maximum accepted intervals.
cost: interval sorting approaches O(n log n); candy standard two-pass O(n) time/O(n) space.
say: “Replacing the first choice in an optimum with my choice cannot reduce the remaining options.”
review: construct a counterexample to the tempting wrong sorting key. Do not assign GR-04 an algorithm until its exact alphabet/rules are known.

title: Sliding windows
conceptCue: maintain a contiguous range whose validity can be restored monotonically.
pitfalls: using windows for arbitrary signed sums, stale frequencies, count versus length, shrinking too little or too far.
cost: standard solutions O(n) expected time with alphabet-sized or O(n) storage; explain why each pointer advances at most n times.
say: “After shrinking, the window satisfies this invariant.”
review: contrast at-most K and exactly K counting; verify any stale-maximum optimization before relying on it.

title: Stacks, queues, deques and cache structure
conceptCue: nearest greater/smaller boundaries use a monotonic stack; a moving maximum uses a deque; LRU combines order and lookup.
pitfalls: indexes versus values, equal-element ties, expired deque elements, circular iteration and linked-list bookkeeping.
cost: stack/deque scans O(n) amortized; Min Stack O(1) operations; LRU expected O(1) operations with O(capacity) space.
say: “An element popped now can never become useful later because…”
review: count pushes/pops and explain the data structure invariant.

title: Heaps
conceptCue: repeatedly retain or extract an extreme without fully sorting. All three source representatives: Heap Sort (HP-01), K-th Largest array (HP-02), Kth Largest stream (HP-03). **Pitfalls:** min-heap versus max-heap, duplicates, k greater than current size, treating heap iteration as sorted. **Cost:** maintaining top k costs O(n log k) time/O(k) space; stream insertion O(log k); heap sort O(n log n) time and can use O(1) auxiliary array space. **Say:** “The root is the worst element among the candidates I keep.” **Review:** trace one insertion and explain why the heap has k elements.
pitfalls: min-heap versus max-heap, duplicates, k greater than current size, treating heap iteration as sorted.
cost: maintaining top k costs O(n log k) time/O(k) space; stream insertion O(log k); heap sort O(n log n) time and can use O(1) auxiliary array space.
say: “The root is the worst element among the candidates I keep.”
review: trace one insertion and explain why the heap has k elements.

title: Binary trees
conceptCue: define a subtree answer and combine children, or traverse levels.
pitfalls: returning the wrong quantity, counting nodes versus edges, treating a tree as a BST, deep recursion.
cost: standard single-pass solutions O(n), DFS O(h) stack or BFS O(w) queue; naïvely recomputing heights for diameter can become O(n²).
say: “This function returns subtree height, while the best complete path is updated separately.”
review: use skewed and branching trees and state exactly what every call returns.

title: Binary search trees
conceptCue: values constrain which subtree can hold an answer; inorder visits sorted values under the chosen duplicate policy.
pitfalls: assuming balanced height, local-only validation and unclear duplicate policy.
cost: search/LCA O(h), potentially O(n); inorder kth selection O(h+k) until found; standard iterator next O(1) amortized/O(h) storage.
say: “Both targets lie on this side according to ordering, so the other subtree is irrelevant.”
review: compare the same query on a generic tree and a skewed BST.

title: Graph traversal and dependencies
conceptCue: reachability, components, unweighted propagation and prerequisites use BFS/DFS or indegrees.
pitfalls: disconnected graphs, marking visited too late, directed versus undirected cycle rules, confusing a BFS layer with a node count.
cost: adjacency-list traversal O(V+E) time/O(V) auxiliary storage; grids O(rc); graph representation itself costs O(V+E).
say: “A node enters the queue only when this condition becomes true.”
review: manually trace a disconnected graph, a cycle and a multi-source grid.

title: Weighted paths, DSU and graph structure
conceptCue: edge weights change shortest-path tools; connectivity under unions suggests DSU.
pitfalls: Dijkstra with negative edges, confusing MST with shortest paths, overflow at infinity, treating DSU as directed reachability.
cost: heap Dijkstra O((V+E) log V) for nonnegative weights, Bellman Ford O(VE), Floyd Warshall O(V³)/O(V²) space, optimized DSU amortized O(α(V)) per operation.
say: “The input property that makes this algorithm valid is…”
review: choose from constraints before coding; Dijkstra, DSU and MST are now core extensions after F14, while the other graph methods remain selective.

title: DP on sequences of positions and grids
conceptCue: overlapping subproblems arise when future choices depend on a small state.
pitfalls: copying a recurrence without defining state, wrong boundary values, mixing negative values with zero defaults.
cost: basic 1D cases O(n) time with O(1) possible space; simple grid cases O(rc) with O(c) possible space.
say: “dp[i] means exactly…, and the final choice can only have come from…”
review: derive recursion, memoization and table order before space optimization.

title: DP on capacity, stock state and subsets
conceptCue: remaining capacity/amount or holding/transaction state determines valid future choices.
pitfalls: counting combinations versus permutations, reuse versus single use, loop direction, impossible states and target assumptions.
cost: amount/capacity DP commonly O(nA) or O(nW) and pseudo-polynomial; unlimited-stock two-state DP O(n).
say: “This state records what is still available, and this transition does/does not permit reuse.”
review: change one rule and explain which transition breaks.

title: DP on pairs, subsequences and intervals
conceptCue: two prefixes, a subsequence ending at an index, or a final split determines a reusable state.
pitfalls: substring versus subsequence, interval boundaries, LIS tie handling and prematurely memorizing advanced formulas.
cost: classic LCS/edit O(nm); basic LIS O(n²), a separate tails method O(n log n); common interval DP O(n³)/O(n²) space.
say: “Conditioning on this last match/operation/split makes the remaining subproblems independent.”
review: develop LCS, Edit Distance and LIS after simpler states; keep advanced interval work parked unless the target requires it.

title: String matching and tries
conceptCue: reuse information about matched prefixes, share dictionary prefixes or choose bits greedily through a trie.
pitfalls: hash collisions, confusing border length with position, terminal markers and missing eligible query elements.
cost: KMP O(n+m); Rabin Karp can degrade to O(nm) when verifying many collisions; trie construction O(total characters), fixed-bit traversal O(b) per item/query before sorting costs where required.
say: “The prefix information lets me avoid comparing these characters again.”
review: C until core string/map work and problem-specific need justify it.
